public_rationale: The broad claim overstates the secrecy. Waymo’s 2020 paper explained what remote assistants could do and how their role differed from driving. Before the post, Cruise had also publicly described remote advisors helping vehicles handle emergency scenes. These were substantive explanations of how operators were used. They do not establish that companies disclosed enough to measure their dependence on assistance. A narrower claim about missing intervention rates would require a separate assessment.
limitations: The result depends on reading the claim as about disclosure of operators’ roles, rather than complete quantitative transparency.
Cruise’s disclosure is documented through contemporaneous reporting because the original page could not be retrieved.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Driverless car companies in general have disclosed almost nothing publicly about their use of remote operators.

statement.document_title: Could Cruise be the Theranos of AI? And is there a dark secret at the core of the entire driverless car industry?

from_speaker: how any of the driverless car companies are using remote operators
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that substantive public explanations of remote operators’ roles were almost nonexistent across the industry.
Descriptions of operators’ tasks, capabilities and limits count as disclosure. They need not establish intervention frequency or performance without assistance.
The target is the cumulative disclosure record available before the original November 4, 2023 post. No starting date is specified because the claim concerns information already made public.
criteria.support_condition: The historical record contains only isolated, vague acknowledgments of remote operators, without substantive explanations across major companies.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Multiple major companies had publicly explained substantive aspects of remote operators’ roles, capabilities or limits before the post.
